items.title: Awaab's Law comes into force in Scotland with strict damp and mould deadlines
items.summary: As reported by STV News, Awaab's Law came into force in Scotland on 6 October 2026 under the Investigation and Commencement of Repair (Scotland) Regulations 2026, for social and private landlords. Damp or mould must be investigated within ten working days, written findings given within three, and repairs started within five, with social tenants' repairs completed within twenty working days.

items.title: Company director wins Upper Tribunal appeal over HMO financial penalty
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the Upper Tribunal allowed a company director's appeal against a financial penalty for HMO regulation breaches. Judge Cooke held that director liability under section 251 of the Housing Act 2004 needs actual knowledge, so being sole director is not enough, and fault lay with the tribunal double-counting where director and company were both penalised.

items.title: Government unveils £16m Legal Support Grant for people facing eviction and debt
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the government has announced a 16 million pound Legal Support Grant for 48 frontline organisations to provide free legal advice to people facing eviction, debt, benefit disputes and family breakdown. Run by the Access to Justice Foundation to March 2029, it funds charities including Citizen's Advice and Shelter Cymru, aiming to resolve problems before court.

items.title: Regulator of Social Housing tells two councils significant improvement is needed
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the Regulator of Social Housing has given Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Thanet District Council a C3 grade after serious failings against its consumer standards. For Nuneaton and Bedworth the issues concern repairs, health and safety and transparency; for Thanet, the condition of homes and anti-social behaviour.

items.title: Councils to get new powers to refer homeless households to social housing providers
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the government will amend the Social Housing Bill to let councils refer homeless households to private registered providers of social housing. The measure aims to reduce reliance on temporary accommodation, and a new Duty to Collaborate will require public services to prevent homelessness. The disposals notification period also extends to eight weeks.

items.title: Practice direction for digital possession claims comes into force
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the practice direction for possession proceedings is now in force, setting out the procedure for claims issued through the new digital possession service. In this first phase it applies to registered social landlords in England bringing claims in postcode areas served by the County Courts at Bradford, Huddersfield and Wandsworth. Wales joins from 15 October.

items.title: Council proposes ban on tenants recording staff without consent
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, Wigan Council is consulting on tenancy agreement changes that would stop residents recording council officers, contractors or agents without express consent, in effect banning video doorbells set to record automatically. The proposals would also bar CCTV in communal areas. The consultation runs until 19 October and has drawn criticism over resident security.

items.title: Government to cut EDMO qualifying period to six months
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the government plans to cut the qualifying period for Empty Dwelling Management Orders from two years to six months. EDMOs let a council manage a long-term empty property for up to seven years while the owner keeps title. The reforms ease evidential requirements, making an EDMO simpler to secure via the Residential Property Tribunal.

items.title: Allocation to track when enforcing disrepair settlements
items.summary: As reported by Local Government Lawyer, the Designated Civil Judge on appeal in S v HA held that CPR rule 26.9(1)(b) still applies when a tenant enforces a compromise over outstanding disrepair works, even though framed as breach of contract. The small claims track is not automatic where the tenant seeks repairs and damages above 1,000 pounds. Allocation matters in settled disrepair claims.

items.title: Use costs to clamp down on 'AI slop', urges former lord chancellor
items.summary: As reported by the Law Society Gazette, former lord chancellor Sir Robert Buckland KC has suggested judges use the costs regime to deter litigants in person from flooding courts with AI-generated material. He said AI has removed the natural brake on prolixity because generating documents costs the filer almost nothing, so AI-generated conduct should still count as conduct under the costs rules.

items.title: Law centres axe service as funding squeeze tightens
items.summary: As reported by the Law Society Gazette, South West London Law Centres has disbanded its employment team and warned its housing team is at risk amid a staff exodus and cuts to external funding. The group is increasingly reliant on grant funding because of legal aid cuts and loss of funding from the Equalities and Human Rights Commission and local authorities.

items.title: Poor records weaken landlords' mould defence, barrister says
items.summary: As reported by Property118, property barrister Jeffrey Zitron of The Barrister Group Chambers says landlords lose most damp and mould disputes through how they handle complaints rather than the law itself. Those who cannot show when a property was last inspected are worse placed to contest a tenant's claim. Damp and mould drives most of the chambers' disrepair work.
